about: Seal of Approval puts the blissful seal photo to work as an old-school advice animal: a fluffy grey seal shot so close its face fills the frame, eyes shut, muzzle bunched into a contented grin. The name is a pun, since the seal literally hands out its approval to whatever the caption describes. Classic entries read like tiny diary confessions of a perfect moment, delivered in the two-line setup and payoff style of 2010s image macros. The seal's smug calm makes even a gross or petty win sound like a refined pleasure.
origin: The photograph was uploaded to Flickr in 2007 and was later captioned as an advice animal on sites like Reddit, where the gratifying-moment captions earned it the punny Seal of Approval name.
usage:
Write the situation in the top box and the rewarding detail in the bottom box, in the clipped style of classic advice animals: "first wipe" / "clean toilet paper", "cold side of the pillow" / "both sides". No punctuation needed.

The captions that do best are oddly satisfying experiences everyone knows but rarely says out loud. Slightly gross or embarrassingly petty is fine; that contrast with the dignified seal is part of the appeal. Since the pun is approval, you can also use it to formally endorse something: a fix, a recipe, a teammate's play.
